newsitem.title: USA: Money managers more neutral on U.S. debt - survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers more neutral on U.S. debt - survey.

text.p: Money managers took more neutral positions in U.S. debt markets in the past week, accoding to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"There was a move back to, or at least toward, neutrality in the survey," the report said.
In the week ended February 11, duration bogey held steady at 4.15 on an arithmetic basis and dropped to 4.69 from 4.70 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index rose to 5.37 from 5.21 on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 5.02 from 4.9 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.16 percent from 7.21 percent.
Eight percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 12 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active rose to 7.0 from 5.67 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
